Intetics Inc. is a global technology company providing custom software development, dedicated team building, software quality assessment, and digital solutions. Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

Being on our team means being part of lasting progress to create a thriving and more sustainable world for our climate and communities. The preparation of environmental documents needed to obtain the environmental authorization of projects), both directly and/or by external services, required for the assessment of the impacts on the environmental and social matrices;
To identify the environmental constraints of the site. To contribute to the preparation of the Feasibility Studies and Due Diligence Analysis;
The environmental constraints check, in relation to new power plants, in order to comply with the environmental authorizations obtained and to define the related Capex or Opex;
To design and perform environmental monitoring on site.

Address the relevant environmental specialized topics for all project development stages (development, permitting and construction phases) in order to ensure the compliance with company environmental best practices, technical specifications, guidelines and general objectives.
Ensure high level competence on authorization issues of renewable power plants, defining and updating the technical specifications needed for the execution of documents for environmental authorization, supporting and assisting any other involved unit within the Organization.

Management/control of external contractors for the execution, for renewable energy power plants, of:
environmental assessment (and eventual integrative documents)
environmental monitoring on site (permitting/construction/operation phases)

Lead, perform and support the other units estimating the costs for the environmental activities to be executed during construction of renewable power plants (wind, solar, geo, Hydro and storage), in relation to own field of expertise.
Lead perform and support the other units the risk assessment related to the construction of renewable power plants (wind, solar, geo, hydro and storage) - related to own field of expertise.
Develop, create and update on a regular basis the technical specifications to be used for any RFPs to be issued by the Organization - related to own field of expertise.
Lead, perform and support the other units for the preparation of the technical evaluation of the offers submitted by the Vendors for any RFPs sent out by the Organization - related to own field of expertise.
Manage, with the support of other units within the Organization, the environmental engineering service contracts.
Support other units within the Organization for the management and supply contracts entered into with external service providers related to own field of expertise.
Support the younger members of the organization.

Ability to work within a Global Framework
Ability to work within a Matrix Organization
Ability in working within multidisciplinary and multicultural teams
Ability to prepare the Technical Specifications for the negotiation of the external services required
Ability to manage and supervise the external Contractors for environmental activities, and to verify their compliance with the Technical Specifications and Best Practices
Development (directly and by management/supervision of “third parties”) of all the documents needed for the Environmental authorization of power plants
Planning and management of environmental authorization activities
Proactivity and flexibility to work in a dynamic environment
Excellent teamwork, coordination, detail orientation and communication skills (written & oral)
Willingness to accept autonomy and responsibility with clear thinking and problem solving abilities
Innovation and Sustainable thinking
Strong organizational and problem solving skills
Effective verbal and written communication
Organizational skills and attention to detail
Ability to work in autonomy for complex tasks and in multiple projects under pressure
Advanced time management and planning skills with ability to review, compile and track project documentation
Availability to travel

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Engineering (or other Scientific Bachelor Degrees related to Environmental). Master's degree preferably in Environmental Engineering or Environmental Sciences, or in other technical/scientific similar faculties
Master’s Degree is preferred
4+ years of experience in the role
General knowledge in renewables power plants processes
Knowledge of the norms/laws for Environmental Permitting of renewable power plants, both, in the country and in agreement to IFC Standards
Techniques for the development of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments, Environmental Assessments of special protected areas, Monitoring Plans (noise, biologic, birds & bats, etc.) during construction and operation
Fluent English is required, Italian or Spanish preferred
Valid Driver's license
Knowledge of informatics:
Microsoft Office
Autocad
GIS Software

Moffitt Services is a leading Texas-based bulk fuel and lubricants distributor headquartered in Cypress, Texas, with a legacy dating back to 1947. We specialize in providing high-quality fuels, lubricants, and superior service to a diverse range of industries, including construction, agriculture, transportation, energy, and emergency response sectors. As a privately held company focused on trust, innovation, and customer-centric growth, we are poised for expansion in a dynamic energy and logistics landscape.

Moffitt Companies are built on generations of family values that stand for superior service. We deliver the right products and services on time, every time, no matter the conditions. Our goal is to serve as a “One Call Does It All” partner dedicated to helping our customers succeed while continuing to grow our legacy of service nationwide.

Position Overview

Moffitt Services is seeking a Director of Environmental, Health, and Safety who will lead the company's comprehensive EHS program. This hands-on leadership role combines strategic direction with active field presence to drive safety culture, ensure regulatory compliance, minimize risks, and foster continuous improvement across operations, fleets, terminals, and facilities.

Lead and manage the Environmental, Health, and Safety department, including building, organizing, and developing a high-performing team; define roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
Serve as a proactive self-starter who identifies opportunities, pushes forward EHS initiatives, and drives implementation of programs to achieve zero-incident goals, regulatory excellence, and operational efficiency.

Lead incident investigations, root cause analyses, corrective/preventive actions, and follow-up to prevent recurrence; manage reporting and documentation for internal and regulatory purposes.
Track and analyze EHS metrics, inspection results, audit findings, training completion, incident trends, and environmental performance to drive accountability, reporting, and strategic decision-making.
Ensure daily operational compliance with DOT regulations for hazardous materials transportation, OSHA standards for workplace safety, TCEQ requirements (e.g., petroleum storage tanks, air permitting, spill prevention/control, emissions from fuel handling), and other applicable environmental/health/safety rules.
Develop and maintain emergency response plans, spill prevention/countermeasure plans (SPCC), and preparedness programs; coordinate drills and response activities.
Manage environmental programs including hazardous waste handling, storage tank compliance, air/water permitting, emissions monitoring, and sustainability initiatives to reduce environmental impact.

Foster a strong, visible culture of safety, environmental stewardship, and health awareness through daily engagement, leadership presence in the field, monthly safety meetings, toolbox talks, and cross-functional collaboration.

Who We Are

Enel North America is a proven renewables leader delivering clean, flexible and sustainable energy solutions.

As part of the Enel Group, we develop, build, own and operate renewable power plants and demand response solutions, with over 11 gigawatts (GW) of installed wind and solar capacity, over 1 GW of energy storage and nearly 5 GW of demand response in the US and Canada.

For nearly 25 years, we've reliably powered modern life and driven climate action with our people, partners and communities by putting sustainability at the center of everything we do. Enel is a top-five industry leader for clean power capacity in the US, demand response in North America and utility-scale battery storage in Texas.

We are a smart and passionate team working together to build the Enel North America that we want for the long-term – one that is founded on strong financial, social and environmental values. Being on our team means being part of lasting progress to create a thriving and more sustainable world for our climate and communities. It means valuing safety, trust, innovation, proactivity, flexibility and respect in all we do. Our vision is ambitious, and we'll get there together.

The Opportunity:

The position, in cooperation with other Units and while also supporting other members will ensure the execution of the activities related to:

The preparation of environmental documents needed to obtain the environmental authorization of projects), both directly and/or by external services, required for the assessment of the impacts on the environmental and social matrices;
To identify the environmental constraints of the site. To contribute to the preparation of the Feasibility Studies and Due Diligence Analysis;
The environmental constraints check, in relation to new power plants, in order to comply with the environmental authorizations obtained and to define the related Capex or Opex;
To design and perform environmental monitoring on site.

The Lead Environmental Engineer will address and solve technical issues related to own field of expertise and by means of own knowledge in order to meet project/authorization requirements.. Those activities could be performed also managing external resources.

Responsibilities, include, but not limited to:

Address the relevant environmental specialized topics for all project development stages (development, permitting and construction phases) in order to ensure the compliance with company environmental best practices, technical specifications, guidelines and general objectives.
Ensure high level competence on authorization issues of renewable power plants, defining and updating the technical specifications needed for the execution of documents for environmental authorization, supporting and assisting any other involved unit within the Organization.

Management/control of external contractors for the execution, for renewable energy power plants, of:
environmental assessment (and eventual integrative documents)

Support the other units within the Organization for the overall planning of the project's activities - related to own field of expertise.

Lead, perform and support the other units for the preparation of the technical evaluation of the offers submitted by the Vendors for any RFPs sent out by the Organization - related to own field of expertise.

Support the younger members of the organization.

Innovation and Sustainable thinking

new_jobs.description:
Director Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS)

Company Overview

Moffitt Services is a leading Texas-based bulk fuel and lubricants distributor headquartered in Cypress, Texas, with a legacy dating back to 1947. We specialize in providing high-quality fuels, lubricants, and superior service to a diverse range of industries, including construction, agriculture, transportation, energy, and emergency response sectors. Our commitment to reliability extends nationwide, offering same-day delivery, 24/7 emergency fueling, disaster relief support, bulk tank rentals, heavy haul services, on-site fueling, and business continuity solutions. As a privately held company focused on trust, innovation, and customer-centric growth, we are poised for expansion in a dynamic energy and logistics landscape.

Mission Statement

Moffitt Companies are built on generations of family values that stand for superior service. We deliver the right products and services on time, every time, no matter the conditions. Our goal is to serve as a “One Call Does It All” partner dedicated to helping our customers succeed while continuing to grow our legacy of service nationwide.

Position Overview

Moffitt Services is seeking a Director of Environmental, Health, and Safety who will lead the company's comprehensive EHS program. This hands-on leadership role combines strategic direction with active field presence to drive safety culture, ensure regulatory compliance, minimize risks, and foster continuous improvement across operations, fleets, terminals, and facilities.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Lead and manage the Environmental, Health, and Safety department, including building, organizing, and developing a high-performing team; define roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
Serve as a proactive self-starter who identifies opportunities, pushes forward EHS initiatives, and drives implementation of programs to achieve zero-incident goals, regulatory excellence, and operational efficiency.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve company-wide EHS policies, programs, and procedures aligned with federal (OSHA, EPA, DOT, USCG), state (TCEQ), and local regulations, particularly for hazardous materials transportation, fuel storage, emissions, spill prevention, and waste management.
Conduct and oversee regular site inspections, facility audits, vehicle inspections, environmental compliance checks, and safety assessments at terminals, field locations, and fleet operations.
Provide hands-on training, coaching, and leadership to drivers, terminal staff, operations teams, and leadership on EHS procedures, regulatory compliance, hazard recognition, safe handling of fuels/lubricants/hazmat, and emergency response.
Lead incident investigations, root cause analyses, corrective/preventive actions, and follow-up to prevent recurrence; manage reporting and documentation for internal and regulatory purposes.
Track and analyze EHS metrics, inspection results, audit findings, training completion, incident trends, and environmental performance to drive accountability, reporting, and strategic decision-making.
Ensure daily operational compliance with DOT regulations for hazardous materials transportation, OSHA standards for workplace safety, TCEQ requirements (e.g., petroleum storage tanks, air permitting, spill prevention/control, emissions from fuel handling), and other applicable environmental/health/safety rules.
Develop and maintain emergency response plans, spill prevention/countermeasure plans (SPCC), and preparedness programs; coordinate drills and response activities.
Manage environmental programs including hazardous waste handling, storage tank compliance, air/water permitting, emissions monitoring, and sustainability initiatives to reduce environmental impact.
Assist with insurance claims, regulatory audits/inspections, and interactions with legal teams by providing thorough documentation and support.
Foster a strong, visible culture of safety, environmental stewardship, and health awareness through daily engagement, leadership presence in the field, monthly safety meetings, toolbox talks, and cross-functional collaboration.
Identify and champion EHS improvement initiatives, including process enhancements, risk reduction strategies, and best practices adoption to support company growth and compliance.

Qualifications

Proven experience in environmental, health, and safety leadership, particularly in fleet operations, hazmat transportation, fuel/petroleum distribution, or related industries.
Strong working knowledge of DOT regulations for hazardous materials transportation (required), OSHA standards, and TCEQ environmental regulations (preferred, including experience with petroleum storage tanks, air permits, spill prevention, and fuel-related compliance in Texas).
Demonstrated ability to lead and develop teams, manage groups of people, push initiatives forward, and drive cultural/operational change.
Self-starter with a proactive, "boots on the ground" management style; comfortable with field work, independent decision-making, and hands-on execution.
Experience conducting field inspections, incident reviews, root cause analysis, training delivery, and regulatory interactions.
Strong communication, documentation, and organizational skills for managing training, inspections, audits, incidents, and compliance records.
Background working with insurance providers, legal teams, and regulatory agencies on claims, audits, and compliance matters.
Experience managing EHS for fleets and operations of various sizes.

Preferred Qualifications

Certified Director of Safety (CDS) or equivalent certification preferred.
Formal education (Bachelor’s degree preferred) in Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, or a related field.
Additional certifications such as CSP, ASP, CHMM, or TCEQ-related credentials are a plus.

Relocation
This position is not eligible for relocation.

Travel Requirements
Monthly travel (3-5 days) is required to provide EHS support, conduct inspections, lead training, and engage with regional locations and field teams.

Work Schedule/Benefits
This position is on-site Monday through Friday. Moffitt Services offers competitive insurance rates through medical, dental, and vision plans; and a 401(k) match program.
